chunks: And it is narrated from Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: "If you come having performed the five salat (prayers), you will not be questioned about any prayer; and if you come having observed the fast of the month of Ramaḍān, you will not be questioned about any fasting."

key_terms.الْخَمْسِ: the five obligatory daily units referred to here as the prescribed daily prayers
key_terms.تُسْأَلْ: to be questioned or held to account
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, whose fasting is obligatory
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ: any prayer beyond what is specifically mentioned
key_terms.صَوْمٍ: any fasting beyond the obligatory fast of Ramaḍān
key_terms.صَوْمِ: fasting as an act of worship

ai.seo_question: If a person performs the five daily prayers and fasts Ramaḍān, will they be questioned about other prayers and fasts?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the central obligation of the five daily salat (prayers) and the sawm (fasting) of the month of Ramaḍān. It indicates that fulfilling these foundational obligatory acts suffices regarding their category, so one is not questioned about additional non-obligatory prayer or fasting.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.614 - It is narrated from Ma'mar ibn Yahya, who said:

I heard Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) say:
"If you perform the five daily prayers, you will not be questioned about any other prayer, and if you observe the fast of the month of Ramadan, you will not be questioned about any other fasting."
